requirements.requirement: Kernel on node1 boots with audit=1 kernel parameter
requirements.summary: Baseline /proc/cmdline (cmd-d7e3dc7c2f654bb6) shows no audit=1. grubby was used to add audit=1 to the BLS boot entry and /etc/kernel/cmdline (cmd-2ef3950b9a8b44d9, cmd-5a607b28f76f479f). After a real reboot (boot_id changed from 31b01b46... to 0d7d2b19..., cross-checked by global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity), the live /proc/cmdline on the new boot includes audit=1 (cmd-1d2f54119bca4c1a, cmd-010f9d75cb16405e), directly confirming the kernel booted with the parameter active.

requirements.requirement: audit=1 setting persists across reboots (not just a one-shot kernel arg)
requirements.summary: grubby --update-kernel=ALL persists the change into the BLS entry file and /etc/kernel/cmdline (both durable, on-disk boot configuration, not a transient one-time GRUB edit), shown in cmd-5a607b28f76f479f. A bounded disruption (systemctl reboot, cmd-3d8a21c872fb48d5) was observed with the node briefly unreachable (cmd-ae8e4bdc288a4d03, connection timeout consistent with reboot), then recovered with a distinct boot_id and audit=1 still present on /proc/cmdline, plus systemctl is-system-running reporting 'running' (cmd-010f9d75cb16405e). This is a full healthy-baseline -> disruption -> recovered-state transition, giving direct evidence of persistence through one actual reboot cycle.

overall_summary: The executor correctly added audit=1 as a persistent kernel boot parameter via grubby (updating both the BLS entry and /etc/kernel/cmdline), and directly verified persistence by rebooting node1 and confirming a new boot_id with audit=1 still present in the live /proc/cmdline and the system fully running. Both material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence, and the single required managed node's restart-evidence protocol (pre-restart boot identity/healthy state, restart acknowledgement, distinct post-restart boot identity, recovered state) is fully demonstrated. No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were found.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was observed; long-term durability across multiple future reboots (e.g., after kernel updates) cannot be directly confirmed, though the mechanism used (BLS entry + /etc/kernel/cmdline via grubby) is the standard durable approach on AlmaLinux 9.

auditd service state was not addressed by the executor and remains inactive on both before and after snapshots; this appears outside the literal task scope (kernel parameter only) but is noted for completeness.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands are directly tied to the task: grubby invocation to set audit=1 (cmd-2ef3950b9a8b44d9) and the reboot to prove persistence (cmd-3d8a21c872fb48d5) are both necessary for the stated outcomes. No unrelated packages were installed, no services were disabled/masked, and no destructive or broad mutations occurred. Lifecycle diff shows only expected changes: boot-identity change, ephemeral systemd-private tmp dirs tied to the new boot session, and listening-socket entries whose only diff is PID numbers after restart (same sshd/chronyd services, no new exposure). No failed services appear before or after. auditd itself remained inactive throughout, but the task only asked for the audit=1 kernel parameter, not for enabling the auditd service, so this is not a gap caused by the executor.
